doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Ella Fitzgerald versus Lena, and early freelance with Slim and Slam
summary: He compares the predictable Ella with the unpredictable Lena and mentions freelancing with Slim Gaillard and Slam Stewart.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Ella was a piece of cake. Incidentally man, I made my first record with Ella, with (Unintelligible)(Slim?) and Slam . That was way back in -­

Well I was playing with Slam Stewart, Slim Gaillard in my freelance days, you know, but Ella -- I could phone my play in. If Ella said (musical sounds) at the end of the eighth bar, she’s going to do that every time so you know what it is, you know what I mean? Lena, you never knew what the hell she was going to do next, you know, what was she going to do. And she never sang anything in the same tempo twice. She could case a room man. She could case a room and she knew whether or not it should pick it up or slow it down or both, you know. She was something else.
